generated git status lists only CHANGELOG.md, docs/source/progress.rst, rich/progress.py and tests/test_progress.py as modified, matching patch.diff file headers.

No registry or __init__ export is required for the feature. patch.diff touches only CHANGELOG.md, docs/source/progress.rst, rich/progress.py and tests/test_progress.py; reference.diff likewise adds no __init__ export (its file headers are CHANGELOG, CONTRIBUTORS, progress.rst, examples/cp_progress.py, progress.py, test_progress.py).

Reader and context classes sit beside track()/_TrackThread in rich/progress.py (generated/rich/progress.py:102-236).

Progress.open and Progress.wrap_file are methods on Progress that drive existing add_task/update (generated/rich/progress.py:1267, :1316), in the same place the reference puts them (reference.diff:545-700).

Shared column construction is centralized in _create_file_progress (generated/rich/progress.py:303-333), which the reference duplicates in two places (reference.diff:377-400, 504-527). This is a reasonable simplification, not an architectural deviation.

Progress tracking goes through the existing Progress API: add_task and update for the task, advance for each read (generated/rich/progress.py:157, :194 seek uses update). Progress.start/stop are reused via _ProgressContext (generated/rich/progress.py:221-232).

Display is built from existing ProgressColumn classes (TextColumn, BarColumn, DownloadColumn, TimeRemainingColumn) in patch.diff:287-301, which is the same mechanism the reference uses (reference.diff:377-391). No parallel rendering path.
_ProgressReader reaches Progress only through its public advance/update methods (generated/rich/progress.py:157, :194), not by touching task internals.
Progress.wrap_file reads self._tasks[task_id].total only inside the class's own self._lock (patch.diff:633-636), the same pattern as reference.diff:576-577.

File-handle ownership is explicit: owns_handle controls whether close() closes the underlying handle (generated/rich/progress.py:188-192). wrap_file passes owns_handle=False (patch.diff:647), so caller-owned files are not closed (tests/test_progress.py patch.diff:786-799).
Repo typecheck gate: base Makefile:7-8 runs 'mypy -p rich --no-incremental'; base .github/workflows/pythonpackage.yml:34-36 runs 'make typecheck' in CI; base pyproject.toml:55-58 sets strict = true.
generated/rich/progress.py:396 declares the module-level open implementation as 'mode: str = "r"', and generated/rich/progress.py:457-466 forwards that unnarrowed str positionally into progress.open.

Progress.open only has overloads for Literal["r","rt"] and Literal["rb"] (generated/rich/progress.py:1171-1200). A plain str argument matches neither overload, so mypy should report a no-overload-match error at generated/rich/progress.py:457. By reading, this makes CI's typecheck step fail. The reference avoids this by typing mode as Union[Literal["rb"], Literal["rt"], Literal["r"]] (reference.diff:458, :626), which mypy can union-match.

The '# type: ignore[return-value, type-var]' at generated/rich/progress.py:467 was written for a different error, and under strict warn_unused_ignores it may also be flagged. Not executed; reasoning from the overloads and config.

Otherwise conventions are followed: Args/Returns/Raises docstrings match the existing style, private helpers use the _Name convention (_TrackThread, _ProgressReader), and tests use pytest with the same Console setup as the existing tests.
criteria.deficiency: The module-level open passes an unnarrowed str mode into the Literal-only Progress.open overloads (generated/rich/progress.py:396, :457-466). Under the repo's strict mypy CI gate (base Makefile:7-8, pythonpackage.yml:34-36) this is very likely a type-check error that the reference does not have (reference.diff:458 uses a Literal union). Fix by widening the module-level mode type to the Literal union, or by adding a suitable overload/cast. Not verified by execution.

evidence: Behavior matches the reference: text for 'r'/'rt' and binary for 'rb' (generated/rich/progress.py:1268-1275); total defaults to os.stat(file).st_size (patch.diff:589-590, reference.diff:675-676); an existing task_id is updated rather than duplicated (patch.diff:592-595); and the progress advances on read, readline, readinto, readlines, and iteration (generated/rich/progress.py:133-190).

Invalid mode raises ValueError before any task is created (generated/rich/progress.py:1237-1239; tests/test_progress.py patch.diff:891-899 asserts tasks == []). A missing path raises before add_task (patch.diff:589-593, test at patch.diff:778-783).

Test coverage is at least the reference's: test_open, test_open_text_mode, test_wrap_file and test_wrap_file_task_total map to candidate tests at patch.diff:700-745, :786-801 and :802-811, and the candidate adds many more. No candidate test is removed.

Minor deviation, shared with the reference: 'tr' passes validation because it is sorted to 'rt' (generated/rich/progress.py:1237-1238), but dispatch checks the raw mode (:1268), so 'tr' returns a binary reader. Built-in open treats 'tr' as text. The candidate's test tests/test_progress.py:827 (patch.diff:947-956) codifies this. The reference does the same (reference.diff:656-658 vs :689), so it is not a regression against the reference.

The reference's examples/cp_progress.py and its 'read' doc example are not reproduced. The reference's own docs reference a 'read' function that its code does not define, so they are not authoritative for names; the patch's names are consistent with its code.
